full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the order dated 20.8.90 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Naria, District Sariatpur, dismissing the Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1989 should not be set aside. 

 3. Against the aforesaid ex parte decree dated 22.3.88 the defendants filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and Miscellaneous Case No. 18 of 1988 was started. From the records it appears that in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case the defendants failed to appear on several occasions. The learned Assistant Judge on three occasions issued notices upon the defendants directing them to show cause as to why their Miscellaneous Case should not be dismissed for default. In spite of giving so many adjournments and also of issuance of show cause notices thrice, the defendants did not care to appear in their own aforesaid Miscellaneous Case and as a result the Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for default on 18.12.88. It is stated that against the aforesaid order dated 18.12.88 the defendants did not take any steps whatsoever and the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 27 of 1987 became final and conclusive. 

 5. The plaintiffs then started Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1989 in the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Naria, for execution of the decree and filed an application under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure for enforcement of the decree for permanent injunction. Plaintiffs deposited all the requisites for issuance of notices upon the defendants. Ultimately, the learned Assistant Judge on 20.8.90 passed an order stating that for executing the decree for permanent injunction the execution case is not maintainable in the eye of law and as such the decree holders were not entitled to get any relief. With the above findings the execution case was dismissed. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid-order dated 20.8.90 passed in Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1989 the plaintiffs preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 6. Mr. Abdur Rab-1, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners, submits that the learned Assistant Judge committed an error of law in rejecting the application under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure and dismissing the Execution Case. He submits that the defendants appeared in the suit, took several adjournments to file written statement, but ultimately no written statement was filed and as a result the suit was decreed ex parte. He further submits that Miscellaneous Case was started at the instance of the defendants on an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit on setting aside the ex parte decree, but ultimately the defendants did not take any steps whatsoever and as a result Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for default. Till today no step was taken by the defendants against the order passed in that Miscellaneous Case. He submits that the decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge for permanent injunction is still in force and defendants are bound to obey the decree for permanent injunction. It is submitted that the defendants willfully disobeyed the decree for permanent injunction and that is why the plaintiffs filed an application under Order 21 rule 32 CPC before the learned Assistant Judge for enforcement of the decree. The mode of enforcement of decree for permanent injunction has been incorporated under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure which runs as follows: 

 "32(1) Where the party against whom a decree for the specific performance of a contract, or for restitution of conjugal rights, or for an injunction, has been passed, has had an opportunity of obeying the decree and has willfully failed to obey it, the decree may be enforced (in the case of a decree for restitution of conjugal rights by the attachment of his property or, in the case of a decree for the specific performance of a contract or for an injunction) by his detention in the civil prison, or by the attachment of his property or by both". 

 Relying upon the provisions of rule 32 as quoted above Mr. Abdur Rab submits that the decree for permanent injunction is still in force and defendants are bound to obey the decree. Since they are not obeying the decree and enforcing it the plaintiffs filed this application under 'Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the learned Assistant Judge for enforcement of the decree as per provision laid down in Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. Mr. Rab submits that in this case defendants have got the opportunity to obey the decree inasmuch as they appeared in the suit, took several adjournments to file written objection and written statement, but ultimately no written objection or written statement was filed and suit was fixed for ex parte disposal and on the appointed day the ex parte decree was passed. He further submits that for setting aside the ex parte decree the defendants instituted a Miscellaneous Case under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In spite of giving so many opportunities and so many adjournments, ultimately the defendants did not appear in their aforesaid Miscellaneous Case and as a result that Miscellaneous Case was also dismissed for default. So Mr. Rab submits that the defendants knew full well about the decree for permanent injunction and as such they had an opportunity to obey the decree but they are willfully disobeying the decree for permanent injunction. Mr. Rab has annexed several papers with this application namely, Annexure B-1, D, D-1, D-2, D-3 and E which clearly show that in spite of knowing about the decree for permanent injunction the defendant-opposite parties are willfully disobeying as well as ignoring the decree for permanent injunction, treating the suit land as part of Chandipur hat although it is a part of homestead of the plaintiff. Further, after dismissal of their Miscellaneous Case No. 18 of 1988 filed under Order 9 rule 13 CPC they are debarred from touching the suit land. So for enforcement of the decree the plaintiffs filed application under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure which was illegally rejected by the learned Assistant Judge. 

 7. Mr. Rab submits that the learned Assistant Judge acted absolutely beyond his jurisdiction in rejecting the Execution Case inasmuch as he had no option but to take steps under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure in view of the fact that the decree for permanent injunction is still in force and the defendants are bound to obey it. Mr. Rab in support of his contention has referred to the case of Sashi Mohan Sen Vs. Ainullah, 1992 BLD (AD) 8. In the aforesaid case the question of enforcement of the decree for injunction came up for consideration before their Lordships. Their Lordships had considered the provisions of Order 21 rule 32 CPC and held as follows: 

 8. From the impugned order it appears that the learned Assistant Judge acted absolutely without jurisdiction in rejecting the Execution Case without taking any action under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Since the decree for permanent injunction still stands good the learned Assistant Judge being Executing Court has no option but to take steps under the provision of Order 21 rule 32 for enforcement of the decree for permanent injunction. So the impugned order of the learned Assistant Judge cannot be sustained in law. 

 9. In this connection the conduct of the defendant-opposite parties needs consideration. The plaintiffs filed the suit for permanent injunction for restraining the defendants from treating the suit property as hat and bazar and also from leasing out the same in auction to any person. The plaintiffs obtained the order of ad-interim injunction and ultimately temporary injunction. The defendants in fact did neither contest the application for injunction nor the suit and as a result the plaintiffs obtained ex parte decree for permanent injunction. It can be further noted that the defendants filed an application under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and a Miscellaneous Case was started but the defendants did not care to take appropriate steps and the learned Assistant Judge, after giving them sufficient opportunity, dismissed the Miscellaneous Case for default. The plaintiffs also issued notice through the learned Advocate informing the defendants about the decree for permanent injunction and to obey the same. Even then the defendant opposite parties are ignoring and disobeying the decree for permanent injunction willfully. 

 10. In this case a question may arise whether the suit for permanent injunction is at all maintainable or not. In this connection it may be noted that after filing the suit for permanent injunction the plaintiffs filed an application for temporary injunction with a prayer for ad-interim injunction claiming exclusive possession and title over the suit land. Ad-interim injunction was granted. Then the defendant-opposite parties took several adjournments to file written objection, but no written objection was filed challenging and/or denying the possession and title of the plaintiffs over the suit land. Ultimately ad-interim injunction was made absolute and temporary injunction was granted within the knowledge of the defendant opposite parties. Thereafter several adjournments were taken by the said defendants to file written statement, but ultimately no written statement was filed by them challenging and denying the averments of the plaint including the claim of title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property and as a result the suit was decreed ex parte. Even before this Court in the present Rule the defendant-opposite-parties did not appear and challenge the title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land. From the above I am of the view that the plaintiffs have been in continuous possession of the suit land and as such their suit for permanent injunction is maintainable. 

 11. Since the decree for permanent injunction is still in force the Executing Court has no option but to take legal steps as contemplated under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure, but without doing that the learned Assistant Judge illegally dismissed the Execution case. Mr. Rab submits that since the defendant opposite parties came to know about the decree for permanent injunction they are bound to obey and enforce it and as they are not obeying it and are willfully ignoring the decree for permanent injunction the Executing Court is bound to take action under the provisions of Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure. I find force in the above contention of Mr. Rab. It appears that the defendant-opposite parties have got sufficient opportunity to obey the decree but they willfully failed to obey it and as such an action under Order 21 rule 32 of the Code of Civil Procedure is called for in the present case. 

 14. In the result, this rule is made absolute without cost and the impugned order dated 20.8.90 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Naria, in Title Execution Case No. 23 of 1989 is set aside. The learned Assistant Judge, Naria, after receipt of the judgment of this Court, shall issue notice, by name and designation, upon the (1) Deputy Commissioner Sariatpur (2). The Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Naria, Sariatpur and (3) Bhumi Karmakarta (Revenue Circle Officer) Naria, Sariatpur, directing them to obey and enforce the decree for permanent injunction passed in Title Suit No. 27 of 1987 within two weeks from date of receipt of the notice of the Executing Court, failing which the Inspector-General of Police, Bangladesh, Dhaka and the Superintendent of Police, Shariatpur shall get the aforesaid three defendant opposite parties arrested and detain them in civil prison for one month in Shariatpur Jail as per provision of the Order 21 rule 32(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure for enforcement of the decree. The learned Assistant Judge, Naria, is directed to report the matter to the SP Sariatpur and Inspector General of Police, Bangladesh, immediately if his notice is not complied with by the above defendant-opposite parties within the stipulated time.
